cladu: cladu (claddu) — to bury; to dig; verbal noun (daruot … cladu penn Bendigeiduran 'finished burying the head of Bendigeidfran'); no mutation (object of the verbal noun follows it)
manauydan: Proper name — Manawydan (u spells w), son of Llŷr, brother of Bendigeidfran; radical, subject after a wnaeth (edrych a wnaeth Manauydan 'Manawydan looked')
hiraeth: hiraeth (hiraeth) — longing, grief, homesickness; noun m.; no mutation of h- after a 'and' (alar a hiraeth 'grief and longing')
uit: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperative 'let it be' (bit); soft-mutated (b>u, = f) after the negative na (na uit kyn drymhet 'let it not be so heavy')
drymhet: trwm (trwm) — heavy, grievous, burdensome; equative degree 'as heavy' (-het/-ed ending); soft-mutated (t>d) after the equative particle kyn 'as' (kyn drymhet genhyt 'as heavy with you')
gwnel: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may he do' (kyn gwnel gameu it 'though he do wrongs to you'); radical gw- here, after kyn 'though' (a chyn gwnel)
gameu: cam (cam) — wrong, injury, injustice; noun m., plural camau (written -eu); soft-mutated (c>g) as the object directly after the verb gwnel (gwnel gameu 'do wrongs'); the cause of the mutation is the usual soft mutation of a direct object following an inflected verb
lledyf: lledyf (lleddf) — slanting; soft, meek, humble, yielding; adjective, before its noun (Trydyd lledyf unben 'the third lledyf chieftain', from a triad of 'Three … Chieftains'; which sense is meant there is disputed); radical (unben begins with a vowel, so any softening after the adjective does not show)
boet: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be' in -et (modern boed); after kyt 'though' (kyt boet keuynderw y mi y gwr hwnnw 'though that man be my cousin'); radical
keuynderw: keuynderw (cefnderw, cefnder) — cousin (male, first cousin); noun m.; radical (kyt boet keuynderw y mi 'though he be cousin to me'); see also geuynderw
goathrist: goathrist (no modern form in current use; cf. trist 'sad') — rather sad, grieved, sorrowful; adjective, predicate of yw genhyf i 'it is sad to me, I am sad' (goathrist yw genhyf i guelet 'it grieves me to see'); probably go- 'somewhat' + athrist 'sorrowful', analysis uncertain; fronted predicate, radical
mrawt: brawt (brawd) — brother; noun m.; nasal-mutated (b>m) after uy 'my' (uy mrawt 'my brother'); t spells d
wney: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. present/future in -i (wnei) 'you do, you will do' (A wney ditheu gynghor arall? 'will you do another counsel?'; Iawn a wney 'you do right'); g lost by soft mutation after the particle a (interrogative, relative)
chyny: cyn (cyn) + ny — 'though not, even if there were not', a contraction of kyn 'though' and the negative ny (a chyny bei itti o gyuoeth namyn … 'and even if you had no realm but …'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'; the following bei is subjunctive
wyn: Proper name — Gwyn (in Gwyn Gloyw), father of Cigfa; soft-mutated (g lost) after uerch 'daughter of' (Kicua uerch Wyn Gloyw); gwyn is also the adjective 'white, fair'
enwedigaeth: enwedigaeth (enwedigaeth) — special right, particular ownership, privilege; noun f. (enwedigaeth y kyuoeth y mi 'the ownership of the realm to me'); the exact sense 'title, ownership' is uncertain; radical, subject of bo
mwynant: mwynant (mwyniant) — enjoyment, use, benefit, as against ownership; noun m. (bit y mwynant y ti 'let the enjoyment be yours'); radical after the article y
mynhut: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'you would want' in -(h)ut (phei mynhut gyuoeth 'if you should want a realm'); no mutation shown after pei
caffut: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive / conditional in -ut 'you would get' (y caffut ti hwnnw 'you would get that'); radical after the particle y
uynhaf: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 1 sg. present 'I want' (na uynhaf 'I do not want'); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the negative na
debygaf: tebygu (GPC tebygu; modern tybio) — to suppose, think, imagine; 1 sg. present 'I think' (mi a debygaf 'I think'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the particle a following the fronted pronoun
werendeweist: gwarandaw (gwrando) — to listen, hearken; 2 sg. preterite in -eist 'you listened' (stem gwerendew-) (na werendeweist eiryoet ar … 'that you never listened to …'); g lost by soft mutation after the negative na
ymdidanwreic: ymdidanwreic (no modern form; ymdidan 'conversation' + gwreic 'woman') — a woman to talk with, a conversational companion; noun f. (ar ymdidanwreic well no hi 'to a better woman to talk with than she'); g of gwreic lost (softened) in the compound; vowel-initial, so the softening after ar does not show
er: yr (y) — the article 'the', spelt er (Er amser 'the time (when)', the noun phrase used adverbially; the Red Book seems to read Yr amser); er 'since' is possible but less likely
delediwach: telediw (no modern form) — comely, fair, well made; adjective, comparative in -ach 'comelier, fairer' (ny bu wreic delediwach no hi 'there was no comelier woman than she'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine noun wreic
anuodlawn: anfodlon (anfodlon) — displeased, dissatisfied, discontented; adjective, an- 'not' + bodlon with soft mutation (b>u/f) after an-; predicate after bydy (ny bydy anuodlawn y phryt 'you will not be displeased with her appearance')
phryt: pryt (pryd) — form, appearance, beauty, face; noun m.; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after y 'her' (y phryt 'her appearance')
vynt: wynt (hwynt) — they; 3 pl. pronoun, spelt with initial v for w (Vynt a gerdassant 'they walked'); fronted subject before the particle a, which softens the verb
racdunt: rac (rhag) + wynt — conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'before them' (modern rhagddynt), in -dunt; idiomatic 'on, ahead of them' (a gerdassant racdunt 'walked on their way'), and 'on their account, before them' elsewhere (a lwydwys racdunt 'prospered before them'; dygywys … racdunt 'was galling because of them')
chicua: Proper name — Cigfa (Cigfa), daughter of Gwyn Gloyw, wife of Pryderi; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and' (a Chicua)
harlwyaw: arlwyo (arlwyo) — to prepare, provide, lay out (a feast); verbal noun in -aw; h- prefixed after y 'her, its' (feminine gwled, 'the feast': wedy y harlwyaw 'after its preparing, after preparing it')
kydeisted: kydeisted (cydeistedd) — to sit together, sitting together; verbal noun, kyd- 'together' + eisted 'sit' (dechreu kydeisted ac ymdidan 'beginning to sit together and talk'); radical, as the object of the verbal noun dechreu
tirioni: tirioni (no modern form in current use; cf. tirion 'gentle, kind') — to grow gentle, tender, become fond; verbal noun placed first before a wnaeth (tirioni a wnaeth y uryt 'his mind grew tender'); radical
hoffi: hoffi (hoffi) — to like, be fond of, love; verbal noun (a hoffi yn y uedwl na welsei … 'and liking in his mind that he had not seen …'); no mutation of h- after a 'and'
eiryoed: eiryoet (erioed) — ever, at any time (with a negative 'never'); adverb, here spelt -d for -t (na welsei eiryoed wreic 'that he had never seen a woman')
digonach: digawn (digon) — enough, sufficient, complete; adjective, comparative in -ach 'more complete, more perfect' (wreic digonach y theket 'a woman more perfect in her beauty'); after the feminine noun wreic it is softened, but d also writes dd, so the change does not show
theket: teced (GPC teced; also tegwch) — fairness, beauty; noun f. from têg 'fair' + -ed; spirant-mutated (t>th) after y 'her' (y theket 'her beauty')
thelediwet: telediwet (no modern form) — comeliness, grace; abstract noun from telediw 'comely'; spirant-mutated (t>th) after y 'her' (a'y thelediwet 'and her comeliness')
dywedeisti: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 2 sg. preterite 'you said' in -eisti (-eist + i) (wrth a dywedeisti 'by what you said'); relative a 'what', so the soft mutation of d (>dd) is not visible
dywedwydat: dywedwydat (no modern form) — apparently a noun from dywedut 'say': 'saying, what was said'; the form is odd and its analysis uncertain (Pa dywedwydat oed hwnnw? 'what saying was that?'); after pa it is softened, but d also writes dd, so the change does not show
roessum: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 1 sg. preterite 'I gave', from the stem ro- (mi a'th roessum yn wreic 'I gave you as wife'); softened after the infixed 'th 'you', but r also writes rh, so the change does not show
uydef: bot (bod) — to be; written for uydaf, 1 sg. future 'I will be', a scribal slip (the Red Book has uydaf; compare mi a uydaf just before); soft-mutated (b>u) after the particle a (a minheu a uydef wrth hynny 'and I will abide by that')
difleis: difleis (no modern form in current use) — guileless, free from malice, harmless; adjective (mor difleis a hynny 'as guileless as that'); di- 'without'; the root is uncertain; after mor soft mutation is expected (d>dd), not visible
kyscwyt: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; impersonal preterite 'it was slept' in -wyt (y kyscwyt genti 'it was slept with her'); radical after the particle y
deryw: daruot (darfod) — to end, be over, come to pass; 3 sg. present with perfect sense, 'has ended, is over' (Ar ny deryw o'r wled 'what is not finished of the feast'); softened after ny, but d also writes dd, so the change does not show
treulwch: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, consume, pass (time); 2 pl. imperative in -wch 'spend, pass' (treulwch chwi 'you pass [the feast]'); radical
hebrwng: hebrwng (hebrwng) — to escort, conduct, convey, carry; verbal noun (y hebrwng uy gwrogaeth 'to bring my homage'); radical after y 'to'
lloegyr: Proper name — Lloegr, England (written Lloegyr, Loygyr, Lloygyr); radical after hyt yn (hyt yn Lloegyr 'as far as England')
kent: Proper name — Caint, Kent; after yg 'in' (yn before k), whose g is the written trace of the nasal mutation (yg Kent = modern yng Nghaint)
arhown: arhos (aros) — to wait, wait for, await; 1 pl. present/future in -own (-wn) 'we will wait for him' (Ninheu a'y arhown); radical after the infixed pronoun 'y 'him'
dreulyssant: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, consume, pass (time); 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they spent' (A'r wled honno a dreulyssant 'that feast they spent'; blwydyn a'r eil a dreulyssant 'a year and the second they spent'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the particle a following a fronted object
kylchaw: kylchu (cylchu) — to go round, travel round, tour; verbal noun in -aw (dechreu a wnaethant kylchaw Dyuet 'they began to go round Dyfed'); radical
rodyaw: rodyaw (rhodio) — to walk about, wander, roam; verbal noun in -yaw (wrth rodyaw y wlat 'while roaming the land'); softened after wrth, but r also writes rh, so the change does not show
gyuanhedach: cyfanhedd (cyfanhedd) — inhabited, settled, dwelling; adjective, comparative in -ach 'more settled' (wlat gyuanhedach no hi 'a land more settled than it'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the feminine noun wlat
heldir: heldir (no modern form) — hunting-land, land for the chase; noun m., hela 'hunt' + tir 'land', with tir softened (t>d) in the compound (na heldir well 'nor a better hunting-land'); h- unchanged after na
amlach: aml (aml) — many, plentiful, frequent; adjective, comparative in -ach 'more plentiful' (nac amlach y mel 'nor more plentiful its honey'); radical after nac
mel: mel (mêl) — honey; noun m. (nac amlach y mel 'nor more plentiful its honey'); radical: y here is 'its' (for the feminine gwlat), which does not change m
physcawt: pysgod (pysgod) — fish; collective noun, MW pysgawd (written -awt) (na'y physcawt 'nor its fish'; a physcawt 'and fish'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after y 'her, its' (referring to feminine gwlat) and after a 'and'
tyuu: tyfu (tyfu) — to grow; verbal noun in narrative use 'grew' (Ac yn hynny tyuu kedymdeithas 'and in that fellowship grew'); radical
mynnei: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish, be willing; 3 sg. imperfect 'wanted' in -ei (hyt na mynnei yr un uot heb y gilid 'so that neither wished to be without the other'); no mutation shown after hyt na
ychen: ych (ych) — ox; plural ychen 'oxen', as in the place-name Ryt Ychen 'Ford of Oxen', Oxford; noun m., genitive following ryt, radical
wrogaeth: gwrogaeth (gwrogaeth) — homage, fealty, vassalage; noun f.; soft-mutated (g lost) after y 'his' (y wrogaeth idaw 'his homage')
gwledeu: gwled (gwledd) — feast, banquet; noun f., plural in -eu (modern gwleddoedd); radical after eu 'their' (eu gwledeu 'their feasts')
hesmwythder: esmwythder (esmwythder) — ease, comfort, softness; noun m.; h- prefixed after eu 'their' (eu hesmwythder 'their ease')
honei: o (o) + hi — conjugated preposition 3 sg. fem. 'of her, from her/it' (modern ohoni), written o honei; here 'from it' of the court, feminine llys (o honei y dechreuit pob anryded 'from it every honour was begun')
dechreuit: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; impersonal imperfect 'was begun' (habitual, 'used to be begun') in -it (y dechreuit pob anryded 'every honour was begun'); radical after the particle y
gwassanaethwyr: gwasanaethwr (gwasanaethwr) — servant, attendant, waiter; noun m., plural gwassanaethwyr (ss for s); radical, subject after uei
dwrwf: twrf (twrf; also twrw) — noise, din, tumult; noun m., spelt twrwf; soft-mutated (t>d) after the presentative llyma (llyma dwrwf 'behold, a noise')
gawat: cawod (cawod) — shower; noun f. (gawat o nywl 'a shower of mist'); soft-mutated (c>g) after llyma 'behold'
nywl: nywl (niwl) — mist, fog; noun m. (gawat o nywl 'a shower of mist'; yn ol y nywl 'after the mist'); n does not change after o or the article
chanhoed: kanuot (canfod) — to see, perceive, make out; 3 sg. imperfect 'saw, could see', in -oed like other compounds of bot (gwybot, adnabot) (hyt na chanhoed yr un ohonunt wy y gilid 'so that none of them could see the other'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after na
goleuhau: goleuhau (goleuo; GPC goleuhau) — to grow light, brighten, light up; verbal noun after yn (llyma yn goleuhau pob lle 'behold, every place growing light'); no mutation
edrychyssant: edrych (edrych) — to look, see; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they looked' (phan edrychyssant y ford … 'when they looked the way …'); radical (vowel-initial)
guelyn: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. imperfect 'used to see, saw', for gwelynt (final -t unwritten; -yn is the shortened -ynt) (y ford y guelyn y preideu 'the way they used to see the flocks'); gu- spells gw-, radical after the relative y
preideu: praidd (praidd) — flock, herd, cattle; noun m., plural in -eu (modern preiddiau); radical after the article y (y preideu 'the flocks')
anreitheu: anrhaith (anrhaith) — spoil, booty, plunder; hence goods, livestock, possessions; noun f., plural in -eu (y preideu a'r anreitheu 'the flocks and the herds/spoils'); the exact sense here, 'livestock' or 'possessions', is uncertain; radical after the article
kyuanhed: cyfanhedd (cyfanhedd) — dwelling, habitation, inhabited place; noun m. (y kyuanhed 'the dwellings'; ay ty ay kyuanhed 'either house or dwelling'); radical after the article y; cf. the adjective gyuanhedach
thy: ty (tŷ) — house; noun m.; spirant-mutated (t>th) after na 'neither' (na thy 'nor any house')
aniueil: anifail (anifail) — animal, beast; noun m.; radical after nac 'nor' before a vowel (nac aniueil)
mwc: mwg (mwg) — smoke; noun m., spelt -c for -g; radical after na (na mwc 'nor smoke')
than: tan (tân) — fire; noun m.; spirant-mutated (t>th) after na 'nor' (na than 'nor fire')
chyuanhed: cyfanhedd (cyfanhedd) — dwelling, habitation; noun m.; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after na 'nor' (na chyuanhed 'nor dwelling')
wac: gwag (gwag) — empty, vacant; adjective, spelt -c for -g; g lost by soft mutation after predicative yn (yn wac 'empty')
diffeith: diffaith (diffaith) — desolate, waste, barren; adjective (wac, diffeith 'empty, desolate'); radical
anghyuanhed: anghyfanhedd (anghyfanhedd) — uninhabited, deserted; adjective, an- 'not' + cyfanhedd, the c nasalised to gh after an-; radical in the series wac, diffeith, anghyuanhed
uil: mil (mil) — animal, beast; noun m.; soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after heb 'without' (heb uil yndi 'without beast in it')
kedymdeithon: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion; noun m., plural in -on (modern cydymdeithion) (eu kedymdeithon e hun 'their own companions'); radical after eu 'their'
colli: colli (colli) — to lose; verbal noun (wedy eu colli 'lost', lit. 'after their losing'; yn colli 'losing'); radical after eu and after the yn of the progressive
wyll: wyll (no modern form; analysis uncertain) — contraction of wy 'they' + yll 'all, the whole company', 'they all' (onyt wyll pedwar 'except them, the four'); cf. the known yll pedwar
anniuer: niuer (nifer) — company, host, retinue; noun m.; an 'our' + niuer, written an(n)iuer (an niuer ninheu 'our company, we'); the an- is the possessive and no further mutation is shown
hundy: hundy (no modern form) — sleeping-house, bed-chamber; noun m., hun 'sleep' + ty 'house', with ty softened (t>d) in the compound; radical after the article
ymedgell: ymedgell — ym 'in' + medgell (no modern form) 'mead-cellar' (med 'mead' + kell 'cell', k softened in the compound), written as one word with the double m written once (Ymedgell 'in the mead-cellar'); noun f.; m is unchanged by the nasal mutation after yn
kegin: kegin (cegin) — kitchen; noun f.; after yg 'in' (yn before k), whose g is the written trace of the nasal mutation (yg kegin = modern yng nghegin)
guydlwdyn: gwydlwdyn (no modern form) — wild beast; noun m., gwyd 'wild' + llwdyn 'beast', with ll softened in the compound; used as a collective, 'wild beasts' (neb ryw dim ny welynt eithyr guydlwdyn 'they saw nothing at all but wild beasts'); gu- spells gw-; radical after eithyr
ymborth: ymborth (ymborth) — (1) food, sustenance (y caffom yn ymborth 'that we may get as sustenance'); (2) as verbal noun, to feed, live (on) (dechreu a wnaethant ymborth ar kic hela 'they began to live on the meat of the chase'); noun m. / verbal noun; radical
bydaueu: bydaf (bydaf; pl. bydafau) — swarm (of bees); plural in -eu (a bydaueu 'and swarms', i.e. bees' honey, wild bees); radical after a 'and' (a does not mutate b)
diwed: diwed (diwedd) — end, close; noun m., d spells dd; radical after the article y (yn y diwed 'in the end')
dygyaw: dygyaw (no modern form) — a rare verb whose sense is uncertain: apparently 'have had enough, grow weary, become too much'; verbal noun (dygyaw a wnaethant 'they grew weary'); the Red Book has diffygyaw 'fail, grow weary' here; radical, fronted before a wnaethant
bydwn: bot (bod) — to be; 1 pl. future 'we will be' in -wn (ny bydwn ual hynn 'we will not be like this'); radical after ny (b is not softened here)
kyrchwn: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, go to; 1 pl. imperative 'let us make for' in -wn (Kyrchwn Loygyr 'let us make for England'); radical
loygyr: Proper name — Lloegr, England (spelt Loygyr); softened (ll>l) as the object straight after the verb (Kyrchwn Loygyr 'let us make for England')
cheisswn: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; 1 pl. imperative 'let us seek' in -wn (a cheisswn greft 'and let us seek a craft'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
greft: crefft (crefft) — craft, trade, skill; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) as the direct object directly after the verb (cheisswn greft 'let us seek a craft'); cause the soft mutation of an object after an inflected verb
caffom: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 1 pl. present subjunctive 'we may get' in -om (greft y caffom yn ymborth 'a craft by which we may get our sustenance'); radical after the particle y
lloygyr: Proper name — Lloegr, England (Lloygyr beside Lloegyr); radical (Kyrchu Lloygyr 'making for England'; yn Lloygyr 'in England')
henford: Proper name — Henffordd, Hereford (MW Henford, f for ff), on the English border; radical (hyt yn Henford 'as far as Hereford'; dros wyneb Henford 'throughout Hereford')
kyfrwyeu: kyfrwy (cyfrwy) — saddle; noun m., plural in -eu (modern cyfrwyau) (gwneuthur kyfrwyeu 'making saddles'); radical
llunyaw: llunyaw (llunio) — to shape, form, fashion, design; verbal noun in -yaw (llunyaw corueu 'shaping saddle-bows'; eu llunyaw ar weith taryaneu 'shaping them after the pattern of shields'); radical
corueu: corf (corf; MW also koryf) — saddle-bow, the raised front or back of a saddle; noun m., plural in -eu (llunyaw corueu 'shaping saddle-bows'); u spells f; radical as the object of the verbal noun
wed: gwedd (gwedd) — manner, fashion, way; noun f.; g lost by soft mutation after the feminine article y (ar y wed y guelsei 'in the manner that he had seen')
guelsei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had seen' in -sei (y guelsei gan Lassar 'that he had seen from Llasar, seen done by Llasar'); gu- spells gw-, radical after the relative y
lassar: Llassar (Llasar) — (1) the name Llasar, in Llassar Llaes Gygnwyt (Llasar Llaes Gyfnewid), softened (ll>l) after gan 'from, with' and o 'by' (gan Lassar, o Lassar); (2) llasar 'azure, blue enamel', in calch lassar, which the text derives from the name; there it is written beside calch llassar, and the l shows no cause (calch is masculine)
gygnwyt: Proper name — the epithet Gyfnewid (written Gygnwyt) in Lassar Llaes Gygnwyt, 'Llasar Llaes Gyfnewid'; cyfnewid means 'exchange', but the spelling here is unusual and the epithet's meaning is uncertain; soft-mutated (c>g) after llaes 'trailing' as an epithet noun
chalch: calch (calch) — lime, plaster, enamel; noun m. (a chalch llassar 'and azure lime'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
calch: calch (calch) — lime, plaster, enamel; noun m. (calch lassar, calch llassar, the blue enamel named after Llasar); radical
gwnathoed: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had made' in -oed (ual y gwnathoed y gwr arall 'as the other man had made'); radical after the relative y
gueith: gweith (gwaith) — work, labour, craft, the thing made; noun m., gu- spells gw- (o'r gueith hwnnw 'of that work'; y gueith wynteu 'their work'); radical after the article and after y standing for eu 'their'
geffit: caffael (cael) — to get, have; impersonal imperfect (subjunctive/habitual) 'was got, could be had' in -it (tra geffit gan Uanawydan 'while there was to be got from Manawydan'); soft-mutated (c>g) after tra 'while'
phrynit: prynu (prynu) — to buy; impersonal imperfect 'was bought' in -it (ny phrynit gan gyfrwyd 'it was not bought from a saddler'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after ny and after hyt na
gyfrwyd: kyfrwyd (no modern form in common use; cf. cyfrwy 'saddle') — saddler; noun m.; soft-mutated (k>g) after gan 'from' (gan gyfrwyd 'from a saddler')
choryf: corf (corf; MW also koryf) — saddle-bow; noun m., spelt koryf (na choryf na chyfrwy 'neither saddle-bow nor saddle'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after na
chyfrwy: kyfrwy (cyfrwy) — saddle; noun m.; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after na 'nor'
adnabu: adnabot (adnabod) — to know, recognise, perceive; 3 sg. preterite 'knew, came to know' in -u (yny adnabu pob un o'r kyfrwydyon 'until each of the saddlers realised'); radical after yny
kyfrwydyon: kyfrwyd (no modern form in common use; cf. cyfrwy 'saddle') — saddler; plural in -yon 'saddlers' (pob un o'r kyfrwydyon 'each of the saddlers'); radical after the article
henill: ennill (ennill) — gain, profit, earnings; noun m.; h- prefixed after 'y 'his' (o'y henill 'of his gain')
frynit: prynu (prynu) — to buy; impersonal imperfect 'was bought' in -it, spelt with f for ph (ny frynit dim ganthunt 'nothing was bought from them'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after ny
cheffit: caffael (cael) — to get, have; impersonal imperfect (subjunctive) 'was got, could be had' in -it (guedy na cheffit gan Uanawydan 'after nothing was to be had from Manawydan'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after na 'not'
ymgynullaw: ymgynnull (ymgynnull; MW ymgynullaw) — to gather together, assemble; reflexive ym- + cynnull, verbal noun in -aw (ymgynullaw y gyt ohonunt 'they gathering together'); radical
duunaw: duunaw (dyuno) — to agree, come to one mind; verbal noun in -aw, du- + un 'one' (duunaw ar y lad ef 'agreeing on killing him'); radical
rybud: rybud (rhybudd) — warning, notice; noun m. (rybud a gawssont 'they got warning'; Rybud a doeth udunt 'warning came to them'); radical, placed first before a
gawssont: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 3 pl. preterite in -ssont 'they got', beside -ssant (rybud a gawssont 'they got warning'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a following the fronted object
chynghoraf: cynghori (cynghori) — to advise, counsel; 1 sg. present 'I advise' (ni chynghoraf i adaw y dref 'I do not advise leaving the town'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after the negative ni
tayogeu: taeog (taeog) — villein, serf, churl; noun m., plural in -eu (tayogeu, modern taeogion) (llad y tayogeu racco 'killing those churls yonder'); radical after the article y
ymladem: ymlad (ymladd) — to fight; 1 pl. imperfect subjunctive 'we fought' in -em (bei ymladem ni ac wyntwy 'if we fought with them'); radical (vowel-initial)
clot: clot (clod) — fame, reputation, renown; noun m. (clot drwc 'ill fame, a bad name'); radical, fronted subject before uydei
carcharu: carcharu (carcharu) — to imprison; verbal noun (ac yn carcharu a wneit 'and we would be imprisoned', lit. 'our imprisoning would be done', yn standing for an 'our'); radical

tref: tref (tref) — town, homestead, settlement; noun f. (kyrchu tref arall 'making for another town'); radical as object after the verbal noun; the adjective arall follows
ymossymdeithaw: ymossymdeithaw (no modern form) — to maintain oneself, make a living; reflexive verbal noun in -aw, ym- + ossymdeith 'sustenance, provision' (cf. gossymdeithaw 'provide for') (e ymossymdeithaw yndi 'to make our living in it'); the e before it is y 'to'
dinas: dinas (dinas) — city, fortified town; noun f. (kyrchu dinas arall 'making for another city'); radical as object after the verbal noun
geluydyt: celfyddyd (celfyddyd) — craft, trade, art, skill; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) after pa 'what' (Pa geluydyt 'what craft')
gwnawn: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 pl. imperative / present-future 'let us make, we will make' in -wn (Gwnawn taryaneu 'let us make shields'; gwnawn grydyaeth 'let us make shoemaking'); radical at the head of a clause
taryaneu: taryan (tarian) — shield; noun f., plural in -eu (modern tariannau) (gwnawn taryaneu 'let us make shields'; gweith taryaneu 'work of shields'); radical
prouwn: profi (profi) — to try, test, prove; 1 pl. present/future 'we will try' in -wn, spelt prouwn (Ni a'y prouwn 'we will try it'); radical after the infixed pronoun 'y 'it'
weith: gwaith (gwaith) — work, make, pattern, manner; noun m. (MW gweith); g lost by soft mutation after ar (ar weith taryaneu da 'after the pattern of good shields, on the work of good shields'); the sense 'manner, pattern' is a little uncertain
gweith: gwaith (gwaith) — work, labour, craft, thing made; noun m. (A'r gweith hwnnw 'and that work'); radical after the article y
lwydwys: llwyddo (llwyddo; MW llwydaw) — to prosper, succeed, thrive; 3 sg. preterite in -wys 'prospered' (a lwydwys racdunt 'prospered before them'); ll>l written, the soft mutation after the particle a
kyflym: kyflym (cyflym) — swift, quick; adjective, predicate placed first before oed (Kyflym oed y gueith 'swift was their work'); radical
diuessur: difesur (GPC difesur, also dimesur) — measureless, immense, immoderate, excessive; adjective/adverb, di- 'without' + mesur 'measure', soft m>u after di- (a diuessur a wneynt 'and measureless they made', i.e. they made a great deal)
dygywys: dygyaw (no modern form) — a rare verb whose sense is uncertain, apparently 'grow weary, become too much (for)'; 3 sg. preterite in -wys (yny dygywys y'w kytdrefwyr racdunt 'until it became too much for their fellow-townsmen'); the Red Book has dygwydawd here; radical after yny
w: w — apostrophe half of y'w 'to his, her, their', y 'to' + w, a contraction of ei/eu; here 'their' (y'w kytdrefwyr 'to their fellow-townsmen'); no mutation, since eu causes none
kytdrefwyr: kytdrefwr (no modern form) — fellow-townsman; noun m., plural in -wyr, kyt- 'fellow' + tref 'town' + gwr 'man', tref softened (t>d) in the compound (y'w kytdrefwyr 'to their fellow-townsmen'); radical after 'w 'their'
duunyssant: duunaw (dyuno) — to agree, come to one mind; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they agreed' (yny duunyssant ar geissaw eu llad 'until they agreed on seeking to kill them'); radical after yny
geissaw: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; verbal noun in -aw (ar geissaw eu llad 'on seeking to kill them'); soft-mutated (c>g) after ar 'on'
chlybot: clybot (clywed) — to hear; verbal noun clybot (a chlybot bot y gwyr 'and hearing that the men were'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
bryt: bryt (bryd) — mind, intent, purpose, mood; noun m., t for d (ac y bryt ar eu dienydyaw 'and their mind on putting them to death', the y being eu 'their'); radical
chymerwn: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 pl. future 'we will take' in -wn (Ny chymerwn inheu y gan y tayogeu 'we will not take it from those churls'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ny
adanunt: at (at) + wynt — conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'to, at them' (modern atynt), in -dunt/-anunt (Awn adanunt 'let us go at them'); no mutation
casswallawn: Proper name — Caswallon (Casswallawn, ss for s), son of Beli; radical, subject before a glywei (Casswallawn a glywei hynny 'Caswallon would hear that')
rewin: rewin (rhewin) — ruin, destruction (Latin ruina); noun, here a predicate placed first (a rewin uydem 'and ruined we would be', lit. 'ruin'); radical
uydem: bot (bod) — to be; 1 pl. imperfect (conditional) 'we would be' in -em (a rewin uydem 'and we would be ruined'); soft-mutated (b>u) after a fronted predicate, the relative a being understood
awni: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 pl. present awn 'we go' with the pronoun ni written on, awn + ni (yd awni wrthi 'by which we go to it, we set about it'); the particle yd is used before a vowel
wdam: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 pl. present 'we know' (o'r a wdam 'of what we know'); g lost by soft mutation after the relative a
grydyaeth: cryddiaeth (cryddiaeth) — shoemaking, the cobbler's trade; noun f. (crydd 'shoemaker' + -yaeth); soft-mutated (c>g) as direct object after gwnawn (gwnawn grydyaeth 'let us do shoemaking')
galhon: calon (calon) — heart, courage, desire; noun f., spelt with h (galhon); soft-mutated (c>g) after o 'of' (ni byd o galhon gan grydyon 'there will not be heart among shoemakers'); the idiom ('they will not have the heart') is not certain; the Red Book's o gallon supports calon, though the White Book's h is unexplained
grydyon: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker; noun m., plural in -yon (modern cryddion); soft-mutated (c>g) after gan 'with, among' (gan grydyon)
ymwarauun: gwarafun (gwarafun) — to forbid, refuse, hinder; reflexive ym-, verbal noun, g lost by soft mutation after ym- (nac ymlad a ni nac ymwarauun 'neither fighting with us nor forbidding'); reciprocal sense uncertain
dyscaf: dyscu (dysgu) — to teach, learn; 1 sg. present/future 'I will teach' in -af (a mi a dyscaf it wniaw 'and I will teach you to sew'); soft mutation after a, not visible (d>dd)
wniaw: gwnïo (gwnïo) — to sew, stitch; verbal noun in -aw (spelt wniaw); g lost by soft mutation as the object following the pronoun it 'to you' (dyscaf it wniaw 'I will teach you sewing')
ymyrrwn: ymyrru (ymyrryd) — to meddle, interfere, concern oneself (with, ar); 1 pl. future in -wn 'we will meddle' (nit ymyrrwn ar gyweiraw lledyr 'we will not meddle with dressing leather'); radical after nit
gyweiraw: kyweiraw (cyweirio) — to put in order, prepare, dress, mend; verbal noun in -aw (ar gyweiraw lledyr 'at dressing leather'); soft-mutated (c>g) after ar
lledyr: lledr (lledr) — leather; noun m., object of the verbal noun (cyweiraw lledyr 'dressing leather'); radical
brynu: prynu (prynu) — to buy; verbal noun, soft-mutated (p>b) after y 'its', the object of a verbal noun standing as a possessive before it (namyn y brynu yn barawt 'but buying it ready-made')
prynu: prynu (prynu) — to buy; verbal noun (dechreu prynu y cordwal 'beginning to buy the cordovan'); radical after dechreu
cordwal: cordwal (cordwal) — cordovan leather, fine leather, from Cordoba; noun m.; radical after the article y
ledyr: lledr (lledr) — leather; noun m.; soft-mutated (ll>l) after amgen 'other' (amgen ledyr no hwnnw 'other leather than that'); written l for ll
phrynei: prynu (prynu) — to buy; 3 sg. imperfect/conditional 'would buy' in -ei (ny phrynei ef 'he would not buy'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after ny
guadneu: gwadn (gwadn) — sole (of the foot, of a shoe); noun m., plural in -eu, used attributively (lledyr guadneu 'sole-leather, leather of soles'); gu- spells gw-
ymgedymdeithassu: ymgedymdeithasu (no modern form in ordinary use; ym- + kedymdeithas 'fellowship') — to make fellowship, associate with; reflexive verbal noun (ymgedymdeithassu a'r eurych 'making fellowship with the goldsmith'); radical
eurych: eurych (eurych) — goldsmith; noun m. (a'r eurych goreu 'the best goldsmith'); radical after the article
guaegeu: gwäeg (GPC gwäeg; not in current use) — buckle, clasp; noun f., plural in -eu (peri guaegeu y'r eskidyeu 'causing buckles to be made for the shoes'); gu- spells gw-
eskidyeu: esgid (esgid) — shoe; noun f., plural eskidyeu (modern esgidiau) (y'r eskidyeu 'for the shoes'); radical after the article
euraw: euro (euro) — to gild, cover with gold; verbal noun in -aw (euraw y guaegeu 'gilding the buckles'); radical
gwybu: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. preterite 'knew, learnt' in -u (yny gwybu 'until he knew'); radical after yny
eurgryd: eurgryd (eurgrydd) — gold-shoemaker, a shoemaker who gilds; noun m., eur- 'gold' + cryd 'shoemaker', with c>g in the compound (yn tryded eurgryd 'the third gold-shoemaker', from a triad of 'Three Gold-Shoemakers')
eskit: esgid (esgid) — shoe; noun f. (nac eskit na hossan 'neither shoe nor hose'); radical after nac
hossan: hosan (hosan) — stocking, hose; noun f., ss for s (na hossan 'nor hose'); radical after na, h- not mutated
gryd: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker, cobbler; noun m.; soft-mutated (c>g) after gan 'from' (gan gryd 'from a shoemaker')
crydyon: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker; noun m., plural in -yon (modern cryddion) (y crydyon 'the shoemakers'); radical after the article
hennill: ennill (ennill) — gain, profit, earnings; noun m.; h- prefixed after eu 'their' (eu hennill 'their gain')
llunyei: llunyaw (llunio) — to shape, form, make; 3 sg. imperfect 'shaped, used to shape' in -ei (ual y llunyei Uanawydan y gueith 'as Manawydan used to shape the work'); radical after the relative y
gwniei: gwnïo (gwnïo) — to sew; 3 sg. imperfect 'sewed, used to sew' in -ei (y gwniei Pryderi 'so Pryderi would sew'); radical after the correlative y 'so'
gausant: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 3 pl. preterite 'they got' in -sant (sef a gausant yn eu kynghor 'this is what they got in their counsel, they decided'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
pam: pam (pam) — why; interrogative adverb (Pam y kymerwn inheu hynny? 'why should we take that?'), followed by the particle y
kymerwn: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 pl. present/future/subjunctive 'we take, we should take' in -wn (Pam y kymerwn inheu hynny 'why should we take that?'); radical after the particle y
lladron: lleidr (lleidr) — thief, robber; noun m., plural lladron (the singular has the affected vowel) (y tayogeu lladron 'the thieving churls', lit. 'the churls thieves'); radical
ymladwn: ymlad (ymladd) — to fight; 1 pl. future/present in -wn 'we will fight' (nyt ymladwn ac wynt 'we will not fight with them'); radical after nyt
hedrych: edrych (edrych) — to look, see, look at; verbal noun, with prosthetic h- after y 'her, its' (y hedrych 'to see it', the feminine Dyuet as referent: ac awn y hedrych 'and let us go to see it')

__broaden__.wy: wynt (hwynt) — they; 3 pl. pronoun, spelling variant (heb wy 'said they') · also emphatic 'them' after a conjugated preposition (ganthunt wy 'from them', ohonunt wy 'of them')
__broaden__.bei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'were, would be' (bei ar y gam 'if it were at its step' = at a walk) · also the conjunction 'if' (bei ymladem ni ac wyntwy 'if we fought with them')
__broaden__.uot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun, soft-mutated after a (ef a eill uot yn ediuar gennyf) · also soft as the complement of a verb (a dylyei uot 'that ought to be') · also soft-mutated after y 'his' (y uot yn colli 'that he was losing', lit. 'his being losing')
__broaden__.bot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun (hyt na bo... uot 'so that there be...') · also introducing a reported fact, 'that (it) was' (adnabot bot eu hennill yn pallu 'knowing that their gain was failing'; clybot bot y gwyr 'hearing that the men were')
__broaden__.nac: nac — (1) negative used in a direct answer, repeating the verb, 'no' (Nac attygaf 'I will not'); (2) 'nor' before a vowel (nac ymdidan) · also negative imperative 'do not' (nac arch dim 'do not ask anything') · also Nac ef 'no', literally 'not it', refusing a proposal (Nac ef, heb y Manawydan 'No, said Manawydan')
__broaden__.wlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f., soft-mutated after the feminine article or possessive (y wlat; i'th wlat) · also soft as the object of a verb, with an adverb between (ny welsynt eiryoet wlat gyuanhedach 'they had never seen a more settled land')
__broaden__.e: y — 'his', spelt e before a following consonant or in some spellings: e gwn 'his dogs', e weneb 'his face'; also the preposition 'to' in e uynet 'to go' · also 'her', with h- before a vowel (e hymlit hi 'to pursue her'); the verbal particle y (e deuthum i 'I came'); y of y wrth 'from' (e wrthaw 'from him'); and in e uynyd 'up', e ymdeith 'away' · also the article 'the' (E brenhin, E chwedyl 'the king', 'the news'); 'it' as dummy subject (E doeth im 'it came to me') · also the infixed object 'him' after a (pwy a'e lladei 'who killed him'; a'e guelei 'who saw him') and 'her' with spirant mutation (a'e chladu yno 'and burying her there'); and the y of y gan 'from' (E gan Uanawydan 'from Manawydan') · also in e hun (ehun) 'self, own', unchanged for any person (eu kedymdeithon e hun 'their own companions'; synnyaw e hun 'watching for himself')
__broaden__.tei: tei — obscure word after brethyn llwyt 'grey cloth'; meaning uncertain, perhaps 'of the house, homespun'; editors have not settled it · also tei 'houses', plural of ty (tŷ) (tei y llys 'the houses of the court')
__broaden__.yn: yn — (1) 'in' (yn Arberth; nasal mutation: yn nyblyc); (2) predicative 'as' with soft mutation (yn wisc hela, yn arglwyd); (3) with a verbal noun, progressive (yn dyuot 'coming'); (4) before an adjective, adverbial (yn llawen 'gladly') · (5) yn yd 'to where' (ymchwelut yn yd oed Pwyll 'returning to where Pwyll was') · also yn yd 'as, while, when' (Ac yn yd aeth pawb ym pen yr arueu 'and while all went to arms'; the sense uncertain) · also 'our', a spelling of an (ein), with no mutation (yn anniuer ninheu 'our own company'; yn ymborth 'our sustenance'; yn diuetha 'our destroying')
__broaden__.well: gwell (gwell) — better; comparative of da 'good', soft-mutated as the object of kyuarch (ny chyuarchaf i well it 'I do not greet you') · also soft as a comparative standing after its noun (seith cantref well 'seven better cantrefs'; heldir well 'a better hunting-land')
__broaden__.le: lle (lle) — place; noun m., soft-mutated after kyfryw 'such' (yn y kyfryw le a hwnn 'in such a place as this') · also soft after heb 'without' (heb le idaw 'without a place of his own')
__broaden__.alar: galar (galar) — grief, mourning; noun m.; g- lost by soft mutation after o 'of' (nac o alar 'nor of grief') · also soft after the adjective diruawr standing before it (diruawr alar 'huge grief')
__broaden__.gyuoethawc: kyuoethawc (cyfoethog) — rich, wealthy, powerful; adjective, soft-mutated (c>g) after predicative yn (yn gyuoethawc 'rich') · also soft after holl (Duw holl gyuoethawc 'God all-powerful')
__broaden__.dref: tref (tref) — town, homestead, settlement; noun f., soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine article y (ar y dref 'on the town') · also soft after holl (yn yr holl dref 'in the whole town') and after y 'to' (y dref arall 'to another town')
__broaden__.uanawydan: Proper name — Manawydan; soft-mutated (m>u) as a person addressed, vocative (Kyuodwch, Uanawydan uab Llyr 'rise, Manawydan son of Llŷr') · also soft after at 'to' (at Uanawydan 'to Manawydan') and after e gan 'from' (E gan Uanawydan 'from Manawydan') · also soft after o marking the doer and after y 'to' (o Uanawydan; y Uanawydan), in apposition after ef (ef Uanawydan) and as the subject straight after the verb (y llunyei Uanawydan)
__broaden__.gaswallawn: Proper name — Caswallon (spelt Caswallawn), son of Beli; soft-mutated (c>g) as agent after a verbal noun with o 'by' (goresgyn o Gaswallawn) and as subject after the negated verb (Ny uynhei Gaswallawn y lad 'Caswallon would not wish to kill him') · also soft after y 'to' (y Gaswallawn uab Beli 'to Caswallon son of Beli')
__broaden__.wybot: gwybot (gwybod) — knowledge, discernment; noun m. used substantively (ny bu gystal dy wybot 'your judgement was never so good') · also the verbal noun 'to know, find out', soft-mutated after y 'to' (y wybot pwy yw 'to find out who she is') · also after heb 'without' (heb wybot dim y wrthunt 'without knowing anything of them')
__broaden__.ueint: maint (maint) — size; noun m. (a'e ueint 'and his size'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the possessive e 'his' · also soft after can 'with' (a chan ueint y twrwf 'and with the size of the noise')
__broaden__.gynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice, will; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (wrth y gynghor ef 'by his counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel of') · also soft as the object of a verb (mi a wnn gynghor da 'I know good counsel') · also soft after a preceding adjective (yn y kyuyng gynghor 'in the narrow counsel') and as object (ni a gymerwn gynghor 'we will take counsel') · also soft after wrth (Reit oed im wrth gynghor 'I could do with counsel') and after pa (a pha gynghor 'and what counsel')
__broaden__.gyuoeth: kyuoeth (cyfoeth) — realm, dominion; noun m., soft-mutated after y/a 'his' (y gyuoeth 'his realm') · also soft after o 'of' (o gyuoeth 'of realm') and as the object of a verb (phei mynhut gyuoeth 'if you wanted a realm')
__broaden__.wreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., soft-mutated after a'y/possessive (ymdidan a'y wreic) · also soft after the article, as a feminine noun (y wreic 'the woman') · also soft after predicative yn (yn wreic 'as wife') and as the subject straight after a verb (ny bu wreic delediwach 'there was no comelier woman')
__broaden__.gedymdeith: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion; noun m., soft-mutated as object (yn gedymdeith 'as a companion') · also soft after 'y 'his' (a'y gedymdeith 'and his companion')
